programs.title: Miao Embroidery: History in Stitches
programs.desc: According to legend, during a migration by the Miao ethnic group, a female chieftain wanted to keep a record of all the mountains and lakes she passed along the way. The means she chose of doing so was by stitching the images on her dress. By the time they reached a suitable place to settle, her clothing was covered with embroidered designs. This, it’s said, was the origin of Miao embroidery. As the story tells us, the designs in Miao embroidery are closely related to the natural world and daily life. The Miao people have a special fondness for nature. So, as well as depicting their daily farming and work activities, they copy birds, flowers, mountains, and grass onto their clothing. Over the years, the embroidery of the Miao people has become a written record of their life. The stitches are like characters which, when many of them are combined, become a record of their history, their collected wisdom, and the knowledge passed down from their ancestors.

programs.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programs.desc: Follow traveling host He Tianran as he explores Xizang's many cultural treasures. Take in the majesty of the Potala Palace, discover intangible cultural heritage skills such as Tibetan paper making and Tibetan incense, and experience the plateau's natural wonders in a whole new light.

programs.title: A Diary from the Empire to the Republic Ep.5
programs.desc: This is Xu Shichang, a 'jinshi' which means a successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations. He was trusted aide to Yuan Shikai, known as the "Crystal Fox" for his political cunning. He was deeply involved in some of the defining events of late Qing Dynasty of China. His diaries offer a glimpse into the intrigues, alliances and power struggles that shaped a turbulent era.

programs.title: Nanjing Yunjin Brocade: A Traditional Chinese Silk Craft
programs.desc: Nanjing's Yunjin Brocade silk handicraft tradition dates back over 1,600 years, and is famous for its exquisite materials, meticulous weaving, and vibrant, splendid patterns. Its core technique is executed manually by two artisans working above and below complex, large-scale looms. Using materials such as silk floss, gold thread, and peacock feather threads, they create luxurious fabrics like imperial dragon robes.
